name: the Copperway Khan
story: The Copperway was Fossick's freight road: ore south across the dunes to the coast, salt and money back north, the wagons pulled by Copperajah. The Khan was its last stop before the sea, a walled caravanserai round a courtyard. When the road closed the company turned its haulers loose (Dustback, data/resident_encounters.json, is the last of them, west of here), bricked up the master's store with the final ledger inside, and walked away. The dunes did the rest: the courtyard and the arcades are drowned in sand to the lintels. One hall has been dug out by a salvager from Fossick; the store under it has not been opened.
ground_rule: Every Y is computed by tools/dune_ruin.py from tools/ground.py (the canonical heightmap, rounded). Nothing in this file is a Y except bounds, which the generator's own --report prints and tests/test_dune_ruin.py holds equal to the plan. The sand line S is max(ground under the Khan's outer walls); the Khan's original floor F is S - khan.bury; the milestones stand on their own ground + 1.

site.gate_faces_why: the gate faces the Copperway, which arrives from Fossick to the north (data/towns.json mining_town)
site.seen_from: Fossick, the place a player goes: the Copperway's first milestone, signed, stands at (6700, 5845), 16 blocks outside Fossick's south footprint edge, and every milestone is 36 blocks from the next, so each is in sight of the one before (view distance 10 chunks, server/config/server.properties.example). The tower's lantern at y167 is 19 over the sand; it comes into a client's view distance (160 blocks) from the seventh milestone on, at (6726, 6061), 149 blocks from the tower. At night the lanterns on every second stone mark the road.

khan.why: a square caravanserai 33 by 33 outside: an outer wall, four ranges of rooms 5 deep, and an arcade of 3-wide arches on piers round a 19 by 19 courtyard (the arcade ring at 10 from the centre). Its original floor F lies bury = 4 under the sand line S, so the arches (F+1..F+3) are buried and their lintels (F+4) lie flush with the sand: drowned to the lintels. The ranges' roofs are at F+5, one block over the sand, and the outer wall stands two over it with merlons on top. The buried rooms are left as the dune left them: their sand is the ground's own, never written.
khan.gate_why: the gate passage is the one way in at the sand line: two blocks of air (F+5, F+6) through the gatehouse, the north range and the arcade's gate bay, over the sand that fills its lower half. The gatehouse stands to F+12, copper-trimmed, with merlons.

tower.why: a solid 5 by 5 masonry tower on the north-west corner (the side the road comes from), to F+20 with a copper cap and a lantern on its top: the Khan's mark on the skyline and, at night, its light. Solid, because a hollow dark tower breeds monsters.

khan.weathering_why: one roof block in seven over the buried rooms is gone (sand shows through), and one merlon in five has fallen: a fixed pattern, so a rebuild is byte-identical

hall.why: the south range's middle hall, opposite the gate (the iwan of a caravanserai): the one room dug out. Floor F, air F+1..F+4, roof intact. The salvager camps here among the brass she has pulled out of it.

trench.why: the salvager's cut down through the courtyard sand to the hall's middle arch: three stair steps and the old paving, the only arch of the twenty that is open. Lantern posts mark its head.

undercroft.why: the master's store: a 9 by 9 vault, 4 blocks of air, its ceiling the Khan's own floor level F, under the south-west of the hall and courtyard. It is reached from the hall's west end through a doorway bricked up in plain sandstone inside a chiseled frame (break it), into the sealed stair-head room in the south-west corner (the antechamber), and down a ladder under a trapdoor. Every block of the vault is written, solid or air, with under_fill rows of sandstone beneath its floor, so the Habitat Block's spawn box holds no air but the vault's. Dark by its own story and lit anyway: soul lanterns, which nobody refilled, and no hostile mob spawns by their light.

road.why: the Copperway itself, marked by its old milestones from just outside Fossick's south edge (data/towns.json mining_town footprint max_z 5829) to the Khan's gate: a post every 40 blocks, chiseled and cut sandstone, every second one with the lantern the salvager hangs to find her way home after dark. The first post carries the road's sign. Each post stands on its own ground + 1; nothing on the road is carved.

blocks.rule: vanilla 1.21.1 only, none a spawn condition in data/spawn_blocks.json (sand is one, for Sandygast and Palossand, so the generator writes NO sand: the Khan's sand is the dune's own, the natural ground the build leaves alone). No chests (tools/portals_audit.py records a chest as a Gimmighoul condition) and no beds (a bed sets a respawn point, which the blackout's checkpoints own). Copper is waxed, so the patina stays as built.
blocks.palette_why: the desert's own stone (the sandstone family) for a building of the dunes, terracotta for the store's tiles, and the haulers' copper, waxed and oxidized, on the gatehouse, the tower's cap and the salvager's pile. Vanilla, as the Lopunny house and the Frostpeak camp are: docs/world-building/BUILD_PALETTE.md lists mod providers, and no mod block is needed for this, so the place adds no dependency.

habitat.why: Cofagrigus, the coffin Pokemon, keep the master's store: the knocking the salvager hears through the bricked door. An ACTIVATED Habitat Block in the middle of the vault floor, disguised as the floor, keeping up to 4 alive (the den's and the Lopunny cellar's pattern). spawn_range 4 makes the spawn box the vault exactly. Cofagrigus is a ghost of the desert theme (data/encounter_design.json rules.themes.desert includes ghost), its hitbox 3.3 x 0.65 baseScale = 2.1 blocks fits the 4 of air, and at 43-53 (the south_east_dunes band) every one is past Yamask's evolution at 34 (Cobblemon 1.8.0 yamask.json), so no level in the band is younger than the species.

npc.why: Dessa Varn stands in the dug-out hall, east of the trench's arch, on the hall floor (F+1): the first person a player meets coming down the steps, clear of her camp, the arch and the bricked door. Placed by R18DU over RCON after the restart that loads cobblers_dialogue's classes (the den keeper's way, tools/ursaluna_cave.py npc_placements).

find.why: the master's strongbox (a barrel, scenery) against the vault's east wall, and the ADR-002 cache round it in data/rewards.json: standing beside it grants the find once per player.

bounds.why: every block the pack writes, as the generator's --report prints it; for the integrator's collision check against the other builders. tests/test_dune_ruin.py holds these equal to the plan.
